description: We are Overflowers, a small team working on the Earth System Trend Detective challenge. Our goal: a web app where a student asks a question in plain language (e.g. "Are summers getting hotter in Kyiv?"), an LLM turns it into a variable, region and time period, and the app shows the trend and its statistical significance from NASA data on an interactive 3D globe. We specialize in backend developmen.
summary:
Earth Verdict is an interactive 3D globe where anyone can fact-check plain-language climate claims (like "Summers in Kyiv are getting hotter") against real NASA and NOAA observations.

A simple trend line is not enough for proof: weather noise and a cherry-picked start year can make random chance look like real climate change. In Earth Verdict, AI only translates your question into technical parameters. Deterministic Python code then runs statistical significance tests (autocorrelation-corrected Mann–Kendall and Sen's slope) across five shifted time windows and cross-checks the results with a nearby NOAA ground station. You get a transparent verdict "Confirmed", "Not proven", or "Refuted" - where every number is fully traceable to its source, with zero AI-hallucinated data.

A trend map of Ukraine adjusts for false positives across 570 grid cells, while a 1981–2025 timeline compares each year to the 1991–2020 climate baseline. The app also runs before-and-after impact tests to see if a power plant or lockdown actually changed local air quality (using a 120 km control buffer and placebo dates), and calculates how much global warming specific CO₂ emissions cause.
details:
Live app: https://myhaven.fun

WHAT IT DOES

NASA portals publish thousands of datasets, and tools like Giovanni let anyone plot a time series with a trend line. Yet Giovanni's own documentation warns that a trend line alone is not a scientific conclusion. Earth Verdict turns a plain-language question into a transparent statistical check and an honest verdict, displayed on an interactive MapLibre globe with NASA GIBS imagery (Blue Marble, VIIRS Black Marble, coastlines).

1. CLIMATE CLAIMS

Covers 10 curated variables: air temperature (mean, min, max), precipitation, snow depth, soil moisture and sunlight (NASA POWER); GPM IMERG precipitation and GLDAS evapotranspiration (via Giovanni); and global temperature (NOAA Climate at a Glance).

For each claim, the backend builds a seasonal time series at the chosen point and runs four checks:

- Statistical significance: Mann-Kendall test with Hamed-Rao autocorrelation correction (significance level 0.05, at least 15 years) and Sen's slope with a 95% confidence interval.

- Robustness: the same test on 5 shifted time windows; at least 4 must agree.

- Independent cross-check: comparison with the nearest NOAA NCEI ground station within 50 km.

- Signal emergence: the year the signal rose above weather noise, or how many more years of data are needed.

Verdict: Confirmed, Not proven or Refuted. Example: winter warming in New York has p = 0.023, yet holds in only 2 of 5 shifted periods, so the verdict is Not proven, with about 7 more years of observations needed.

2. TREND MAP AND TIMELINE

Sen's slope and Mann-Kendall p-values for 570 grid cells (0.5 x 0.625 degrees) over Ukraine, with Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate correction. For annual precipitation, 114 cells look significant on raw p-values, but none survive the correction, while summer temperature keeps all 570.

A 1981-2025 timeline shows each year's anomaly against the 1991-2020 normal and its rank (summer 2024: 2.5 °C warmer than usual, the warmest of 45 summers).

3. POLLUTION EVENTS

NO2 and SO2 (Aura OMI) and aerosol optical depth (MERRA-2) via Giovanni for 5 curated events. A before-after-control-impact (BACI) design compares the site with a control ring 120 km away, and at least 3 placebo "fake dates" keep a background trend from being credited to a single event.

4. CO2 CALCULATOR

Using NOAA GML global CO2 data, converts emissions into atmospheric ppm (44% airborne fraction), radiative forcing (Myhre et al., 1998) and transient warming (IPCC AR6: 1.8 °C per CO2 doubling, range 1.4 to 2.2 °C).

5. FUTURE SCENARIOS

NASA NEX-GDDP-CMIP6 projections (SSP1-2.6, SSP2-4.5, SSP5-8.5; 4-5 models) for selected regions, shown as illustration only.

AI WITHOUT INVENTED NUMBERS

Gemini does only two things: it turns free text into catalog-whitelisted parameters and explains the computed results. A backend guard checks every number in the AI's answer against the computed facts; an answer with any unverified number is rejected and replaced with text built by the code.

WHO IT HELPS

Students, teachers, journalists and curious citizens: instead of just a line on a chart, they see whether the evidence is solid, mixed or still weather noise, and why.

TOOLS AND STACK

- Backend: Python, FastAPI, NumPy, SciPy, Pydantic, PyYAML (222 tests)

- Frontend: React 19, TypeScript, Vite, Zod, MapLibre GL JS (95 Playwright end-to-end tests)

- Deployment: Docker, Uvicorn, nginx; disk caching and rate limiting

USE OF AI

- In the app: Gemini handles query parsing and checked explanations only, never calculations.

- In development: AI tools helped draft code, tests, documentation and prompts; the team reviewed and tested all of it.

- Demo video: the English voiceover was generated with AI text-to-speech (FreeTextToSpeech.net) from a team-written script; all visuals are real screen recordings of the working app.
